findings.explanation: This rejects the batch only when none of its documents belong to actorTenant. A requested batch containing both an authorized document and a document from another tenant passes this check, and line 13 returns every document.value directly to the caller. The contract requires every requested document to belong to actorTenant; use an all-documents check so mixed-tenant batches return null.

This only rejects a batch when none of its documents belong to the actor. A mixed batch containing at least one document for actorTenant and one for another tenant passes and returns every document's value on line 13, exposing the other tenant's document. The contract requires every requested document to belong to actorTenant; reject when any document has a different tenant.

This rejects only when none of the requested documents belong to actorTenant. A mixed batch containing one caller-owned document and one document from another tenant passes and returns every document value at line 14. The contract requires every requested document to belong to the caller's tenant, so this check must reject if any document is unauthorized.

This rejects the batch only when none of the requested documents belong to actorTenant. A mixed batch containing one caller-owned document and one document belonging to another tenant passes and returns every document value on line 13, exposing the other tenant's data. The contract requires every requested document to belong to actorTenant; use an all-documents check.

This rejects only when none of the requested documents belong to actorTenant. A mixed batch containing one caller-owned document and one document belonging to another tenant passes this check, and line 13 returns every document value directly to the caller. Require every document to match actorTenant (for example, use an every check); otherwise return null.

This rejects the batch only when none of the documents belongs to the caller's tenant. A batch containing one caller-owned document and one document from another tenant passes and returns every document value on line 13, disclosing the foreign document. The contract requires rejecting the batch unless every requested document belongs to actorTenant; use an all-documents check.

This only rejects the batch when none of the requested documents belongs to the caller's tenant. A batch containing one authorized document and one document belonging to another tenant passes and line 13 returns both values to the caller. The contract requires every requested document to belong to actorTenant; this check must reject if any document has a different tenant.

This checks that at least one requested document belongs to the caller's tenant, not that every document does. A batch containing both a caller-owned document and another tenant's document passes this check, and line 13 returns every document's value directly. That leaks the other tenant's document; the contract requires returning null unless all requested documents belong to actorTenant.

This rejects the batch only when none of the documents belong to actorTenant. Since requestedIds is caller-controlled and returned values go directly to the caller, require every document to belong to actorTenant; otherwise return null.

This only rejects the batch when none of the documents belongs to actorTenant. This only rejects a batch when none of its documents belong to actorTenant. A caller can include one owned ID and one ID belonging to another tenant; the check passes and line 13 returns every document value, exposing the other tenant's data. Require every requested document to match actorTenant and return null otherwise.

A batch containing one caller-owned document and one document from another tenant passes this check, and line 13 returns every document's value directly to the caller. Reject unless all requested documents belong to actorTenant.

The contract requires every requested document to belong to the caller's tenant, so reject unless all documents match.

Reject the batch if any document is not owned by actorTenant.
